canonical_record.title: DAE-Aware Bayesian Inference for Joint Generator-Network Parameter Estimation

uses.context:
Physical stochastic models support latent-state estimation
\cite{ensaf2023kernel,tartakovsky2023gp}, while joint DAE parameter inference
addresses uncertain generators and networks \cite{albustami2026dae}.
Our stream method uses a finite bank of constant network hypotheses.
Trajectory sensitivities and Gaussian evidence have also been combined
for Bayesian parameter inference in power-system DAEs
\cite{nagi2022trajectory}. Their use alone does not distinguish an event
attribution algorithm. The separate signature test examines a local event--context derivative;
it does not identify every plant parameter or replace the stream method
with an unrestricted joint estimator.
uses.note: The abstract explicitly treats joint Bayesian estimation of generator inertia/damping and branch resistance/reactance in a power-system DAE.

canonical_record.title: The interacting multiple model algorithm for systems with Markovian switching coefficients
canonical_record.publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)

uses.context:
The Adaptive Matrix CuSum derives sequential identification error/delay
results under specified observation laws \cite{warner2024matrix}.
Multiple-model filtering already propagates conditional state/mode
hypotheses \cite{blom1988imm}. The multiple-model multiple-hypothesis
filter maintains mode-sequence histories and adapts their number through
pruning and merging \cite{boers2005m3h}. Retaining histories or adapting
bank size is therefore not an original principle of our method.
Our pruned history bank uses these ideas,
but its approximate covariances, proposal screen and fitted startup context
do not inherit their general guarantees. The complete procedure evaluated
here makes retained recovery compete with later interventions and reports
timely attribution and alarm burden. These comparisons do not isolate
recovery memory from the other admission and publication rules.
uses.note: The paper develops approximate Bayesian filtering and hypothesis merging for Markovian switching linear systems, supporting the stated multiple-model precedent.

canonical_record.title: Quickest Line Outage Detection and Identification
canonical_record.publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)

uses.context:
Existing work provides strong foundations. DAE state estimators infer
unmeasured electrical states \cite{katanic2024recursive}; physical outage
detectors compare network hypotheses sequentially
\cite{chen2016quickest,rovatsos2017outage}; and simulated fault trajectories
support diagnosis from sparse PMUs \cite{warner2023highfidelity}.
Physical models, transient histories and unknown-onset searches are thus
established ingredients. A small state-reconstruction error, however, does
not by itself identify the intervention that produced the observations.

uses.context: The published physical comparator is Chen \emph{et al.}'s persistent single-line quickest-change detector \cite{chen2016quickest}. Its reduced-network covariance is marginalized to the observed PMU subset after inversion. Parallel CUSUM statistics stop at the first threshold crossing and select a line. Our declared F01 adapter uses nonoverlapping angle increments at 15 Hz, a startup-only scale/drift estimate and the fixed nominal line catalog. Its white-injection/DC assumptions do not describe all F01 instrumental effects. We preserve both matched-law implementation checks and F01 mismatch failures; no ARL guarantee is transferred to colored noise.

canonical_record.title: A method for quantitative fault diagnosability analysis of stochastic linear descriptor models
canonical_record.publisher: Elsevier BV

uses.context:
\subsection{State Estimation and Physical Source Inference}
Unknown-input and DAE estimators recover electrical states despite
incomplete models or exogenous inputs
\cite{gillijns2007input,nugroho2022dae,katanic2024recursive}. Functional
observability asks whether a requested state quantity can be recovered
\cite{fernando2010functional,montanari2022functional}. Source inference asks
which intervention can explain the trajectory. Descriptor-model
diagnosability and nuisance-profiled tests formalize this distinction
\cite{eriksson2013diagnosability,scharf1994matched}.
uses.note: The source quantifies fault-mode distinguishability in stochastic descriptor models through KL divergence and links it to fault-to-noise ratio. It supports the qualitative source-separation argument, not a universal calibrated error formula.

canonical_record.venue: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
canonical_record.publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)

uses.context:
Existing work provides strong foundations. DAE state estimators infer
unmeasured electrical states \cite{katanic2024recursive}; physical outage
detectors compare network hypotheses sequentially
\cite{chen2016quickest,rovatsos2017outage}; and simulated fault trajectories
support diagnosis from sparse PMUs \cite{warner2023highfidelity}.
Physical models, transient histories and unknown-onset searches are thus
established ingredients. A small state-reconstruction error, however, does
not by itself identify the intervention that produced the observations.
uses.note: The original paper uses simulated voltage/current paths, maximizes over onset positions t-M <= k < t, and returns candidate lines. The evaluated target is short circuits with clearing assumed after the detection window (Section IV.C); load changes are tested for induced false alarms (Section IV.D). Both uses are supported. Direct TechRxiv/PDF access failed, so the full-text mirror and registry were used; byte identity to v1 was not certified.

uses.context:
\subsection{Trajectory-Based and Sequential Diagnosis}
Warner \emph{et al.} compare simulated voltage/current fault trajectories
over a moving onset window and return candidate lines
\cite{warner2023highfidelity}. Their evaluated target is short-circuit
identification before clearing; load changes are an adverse-event test.
Our target follows load changes and line openings through restoration and
successive interventions. Physical trajectory libraries, remote PMUs and
retrospective onset scanning are shared ingredients. Their procedure was
not run on our data, so no numerical superiority is inferred.

canonical_record.title: Sequential change diagnosis revisited and the Adaptive Matrix CuSum
canonical_record.publisher: Bernoulli Society for Mathematical Statistics and Probability

uses.context:
The Adaptive Matrix CuSum derives sequential identification error/delay
results under specified observation laws \cite{warner2024matrix}.
Multiple-model filtering already propagates conditional state/mode
hypotheses \cite{blom1988imm}. The multiple-model multiple-hypothesis
filter maintains mode-sequence histories and adapts their number through
pruning and merging \cite{boers2005m3h}. Retaining histories or adapting
bank size is therefore not an original principle of our method.
Our pruned history bank uses these ideas,
but its approximate covariances, proposal screen and fitted startup context
do not inherit their general guarantees. The complete procedure evaluated
here makes retained recovery compete with later interventions and reports
timely attribution and alarm burden. These comparisons do not isolate
recovery memory from the other admission and publication rules.
uses.note: The source analyzes sequential change diagnosis with a finite family of post-change laws, unknown onset, error control and delay; the manuscript appropriately withholds transfer of those guarantees to its approximate bank.
